newsitem.title: UK: IPO VIEW - Quiet week expected for LSE new issues.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Quiet week expected for LSE new issues.

text.p: Market observers on Friday were not expecting any fireworks from new issues on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) next week with only two modestly sized companies due to float in the next five days.

Dealers blamed the summer holiday period in London for the reduced investor appetite for stocks coming to the market and added fund managers currently seemed more interested in larger capitalised companies than smaller issues.
"At the end of the second quarter we saw switching out of smaller issues and into FTSE 100 stocks," said one corporate dealer.
The larger of the two newcomers is London bus company Metroline Plc which is expected to make its debut on July 29, having raised around three million stg from a placing at 173p per share.
Share dealing in the comparatively smaller Fairplace Consulting Plc is due to begin on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on July 28.
Fairplace, an outplacement and career management consultant, has raised about 765,000 stg and is valued at around 3.7 million stg at its issue price of 3p per share.
